chunks.text: 國立臺灣科技大學 工業管理系 碩士學位論文 學號： M10901814 設計以工業 4.0 標準介面模擬為基的智慧工廠數位孿生 Designing Simulation-based Digital Twin for Smart Warehouse: An Asset Administration Shell Framework 研 究 生：Zakka Ugih Rizqi 指導教授： Shuo -Yan Chou 中華民國 110 年 07 月 ii MASTER’S THESIS RECOMMENDATION FORM iii QUALIFICATION FORM BY COMMITTEE iv ABSTRACT The need for improving flexibility, optimality, and transparency of industry processes increases since the customer demands are highly diverse and full of uncertainty. Cyber - Physical System (CPS) technology now is being developed to meet those requirements.

It can be achieved through Digital Twin (DT). Unfortunately, the application of DT is still limited in practice nowadays, and no stan dard way to achieve integration. The concept of an Asset Administration Shell (AAS) proposed by Plattform Industrie 4.0 arose as a promising concept to realize DT in standard manner . However, the granularity of AAS remains undefined and still under develop ment.

A literature study shows that most of studies only reached static digital twin and only considered a few specific assets especially unmovable assets. Dynamic digital twin is only supported by Virtual Reality (VR) that cannot be used for optimization as well as direct controlling.

Therefore, this research intends to contribute to DT development by proposing 3D computer simulation technology as dynamic digital twin by following Reference Architecture Model Industrie 4.0 (RAMI 4.0) based on AAS Framework . The proposed concept enables DT to do dynamic monitoring, optimization , and direct controlling. As a use case, a smart warehouse in Taiwan is used and assets considered include Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs), Operator, Conveyor, Forklift, and Storage R ack. This research consists of 4 stages. First, AAS Variables Definition, identifying the assets and the data that want to be exchanged via AAS, defining AAS capability and AAS structure.

Second, AAS Simulation Modeling with Flexsim software is established . Third, AAS System Integration consists of designing communication networks and information modeling. And last, demonstrating 2 main advantages of using simulation which are simulation -based optimization for AGV capacity planning and creating dynamic dash board. To support communication between assets, OPC Unified Architecture (OPC UA) and Automation Markup Language (AutomationML) are determined. As a result of demonstration, simulation-based optimization is done for multi-objectives and can find the optimum capacity of each AGV.

Dynamic dashboard is also created to ease real-time monitoring process. Later on, data from dashboard can be exported to database and predictive analytics can be done. Based on these capabilities, industry 4.0 scenarios can be integ rated systematically and comprehensively.

chunks.section: 2. CHAPTER 2 > 2.1. Deductive Review
chunks.text: Deductive Review 2.1.1 Industry 4.0 The fou rth industrial revolution, also named Industry 4.0 (I4.0), will digitalize manufacturing operations and decentralize them from the shop floor to the office and over whole enterprise networks [1]. The main objective of Industry 4.0 is satisfying individual customer needs which influences areas like order management, manufacturing operations, delivery to customers [17]. The four main drivers of Industry 4.0 are the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), Cloud-based Manufacturing, Internet of Things (IoT), and Smart Manufacturing which helps in transforming manufacturing processes into fully digital and intelligent processes [18]. Another stud y also proposes 9 pil lars of I4.0 which are Big Data & Analytics, Autonomous Robots, Simulation, System Integration, The Industrial Internet of Things, Cyber security & Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), The Cloud, Additive Manufacturing, and Augmented Reality [17]. But the challenge is how to integrate those t echnology into fully integrated and provides standard way to implement. Plattform Industrie 4.0 (2016) [19] proposed 9 application scenarios of industry 4.0 to ease understanding of implementation in practice: 1. OCP – Order-Controlled Production: Autonomous and automated interconnection of production. 2. AF – Adaptable Factory: Plug & Produce – adaptable manufacturing configurations within a factory for quickly changing production capacities and capabilities. 6 3. SAL – Self-organising Adaptive Logistics: Increasing flexibility and reaction time of industrial and logistics systems in increasingly volatile and adaptable production environments. 4. VBS – Value-Based Services: Process and status data from production and product use sources are the raw materials for future business models and services. 5. TAP – Transparency and Adaptability of delivered Products: Automatic collection of use-based data from delivered products for optimising business processes, for new busines s models and for dynamic adaptation of product features. 6. OSP – Operator Support in Production: Human -technology-human interaction for assisting humans as actors in the manufacturing process. 7. SP2 – Smart Product Development for Smart Production: Virtual p roducts allow for new types of teamwork in engineering processes and automation of engineering activities. 8. IPD – Innovative Product Development: Sufficiently integrating all relevant stakeholders in the engineering process and using a suitable methodical approach helps to develop the product in the right way. 9. CRE – Circular Economy: High -grade recycling of materials from manufacturing during the entire life cycle of a product.

chunks.text: 2.1.2 Reference Architecture Model for Industry 4.0 (RAMI 4.0) In discussing Industr y 4.0, there is a framework that approaches the issue of Industry 4.0 in a structured manner, namely Reference Architecture Model for Industry 4.0 (RAMI 4.0) proposed by German Plattform Industrie 4.0 shown in Figure 2.1 [5]. Actually, there are also other framework s with the same purpose like Industrial Internet Reference Architecture (IIRA) proposed by IIC from US [20], IBM Industry 4.0 Architecture proposed by IBM [21], and NIST Smart Manufacturing [22]. Compared to others, RAMI 4.0 gives more comprehensive information and more relevant to be implemented in industry especially for smart manufacturing [21]. RAMI 4.0 provides an orientation for plotting the requirements of sectors together with standards in order to define and further develop Industry 4.0 [23]. It is implemented in Industry 4.0 aspects for smart manufacturing which combines all elements and IT components [24]. 7 Since the main challenge of industry 4.0 is interoperability, it is also shown in RAMI 4.0 from architectural layers which are divided into 2 aspects, namely physical aspects and digital aspects.

To change the physical thing to the digital, there is integration layer between asset and c ommunication layers that applies the Digital Twin (DT) concept. Figure 2. 1 Reference Architecture Model for Industry 4.0 (Source: [5]) 2.1.3 Digital Twin The concept of the Digital Twin (DT) came from the presentation in 2002 entitled “Conceptual Ideal for Product Lifecycle Management (PLM)” by Dr. Grieves [25]. It is called ‘Twin’ because it is like mirroring or twinning of systems between what existed in real space to what existed in virtual space and vice versa.

chunks.text: But at that time, internet was still expensive and limited. Since DT uses internet as the basic technology so that the development of DT did not appear. But today, internet becomes cheaper and borderless so that many industries have implemented DT to enhance interoperability across value stream of an asset like shown in Figure 2.2 [26].

chunks.text: The concept of DT will be diffe rent with the other modeling concept even others show like mirroring the physical system. For example, Computer Aided Manufacturing (CAM) is also mirroring the physical system but it does not have capability to connect physical system with digital system w ith bi-directional. This is the main difference of DT concept compared with others. In DT, digital system will be connected in real-time and have capability to control physical system. However, CAM or others concept can also be applied as part of DT. 8 Figure 2.

chunks.text: 2 Development of D igital Twin in 2015 (Source: [26]) Digital twin (DT) is known as the basic concept to support integration in Industry 4.0 and refers to virtual models of an asset that are fully integrated with a real thing/asset [27]. In DT, digital asset and physical asset are connected by internet with semantic relationships. It can be used for virtual testing, analyzing collected data, and predicting future behavior o f physical things before applying it to real things [15]. Since DT has so many advantages, DT can be practically applied in almost every industry like shown in Table 2.1. Table 2. 1 Digital Twin in Practice (Source:[28]) Construction Aerospace High Tech Physical Things Digital Twin 9 Besides that, DT also can solve information silos problems as shown in Figure 2.3. Traditionally, the information about an asset is usually scattered across multiple information sources, which are maintained by different organizations. It will result in du plicated, inconsistent, and missing information. With digital twin, it can collect data centrally for every entity and then makes that information available to different areas of the business for their specific applications through integration interfaces, such as Application Programming Interfaces (APIs ) [29]. This improves decision -making through a shared unde rstanding and reduces the overall lifecycle cost of operating and maintaining a plant . Figure 2. 3 Digital Twin to Solve Information Silos Problem (Source: [29]) 2.1.4 Asset Administration Shell One of the approaches to realize Digital Twin in manufacturing industry is called Asset Administration Shell (AAS) [29].

The asset refers to the physical things e.g. machine, product, & materials, and the administration shell refers to the digital thing that stores information about the asset over its entire lifecycle. The AAS can be understood as software entity providi ng asset’s information to the external by means of a standardized Application Programming Interface (API). In smart manufacturing, each physical thing or asset has its own administration shell, and each administration shell can connect with the other admin istration shell as shown in Figure 2.4 [29]. 10 Figure 2. 4 Concept of Asset Administration Shell (Source: [29]) The structure of an AAS can be isolated into a digital factory (DF) header and body like shown in Figure 2.5 [11].

chunks.text: 2.1.5 AutomationML AutomationML or Automation Markup Language or AML is pointed at accomplishing standardized and efficient data exchange during the engineering processes of a manufacturing system, which can reduce time and cost [12]. The main idea is, instead of developing a new data format for that purpose, AutomationML adapts, extends, and merges already existing standardized data formats in an appropriate way .

chunks.section: 9. CRE – Circular Economy: High -grade recycling of materials from manufacturing
chunks.text: AML has been standardized in IEC 62714. AML is an open and neutral XML -based data exchange format that can be ut ilized for product, process, and resource descriptions within the production -system engineering domain [32].

chunks.section: 9. CRE – Circular Economy: High -grade recycling of materials from manufacturing
chunks.text: The basic structure of AutomationML is shown in Figure 2.6 [33]. The core of AutomationML is the top-level data format Computer Aided Engineering Exchange (CAEX), which connects distinctive engineering data formats, such as Collaborative Design Activity (COLLADA) and PLCopen XML [34]. Moreover, AutomationML has an inherent distributed architecture established on the concept of the object -oriented method, as does CAEX. 12 Figure 2.

chunks.text: 6 Structure of AML (Source: [33]) 2.1.6 OPC UA Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) technology accomplishes message -based communication between clients and servers on different types of networks to facilitate various leveled industrial system information exchange, such as in connection to field devices, control systems, manufacturing execution systems , and enterprise resource planning systems [35]. OPC UA has been standardized in IEC 62541. OPC UA follows client -server system. The OPC UA client uses the client application program interface (API) to send/receive OPC UA service request/response messages (Req/Rsp Msg) to/from the OPC UA server. Here, service is designed to discover the OPC UA servers that are available in a particular system environment.

The role of the communication sta ck is to support data transportation between the client and server, which converts the client API calls to messages and sends them through the underlying communication entity to the OPC UA server [36].

This is the reason why the AML model can be integrated into the OPC UA because the AML metadata can be mapped to the OPC UA nodes in a standardized manner [38]. 2.1.7 Discrete-Event Simulation and Simulation Optimization Discrete-Event Simulation (DES) quantitatively represents the real world, simulates its dynamics on an event -by-event under uncertainty, and generates detailed performance report based on simulation. It has become one of the mainstream computer -aided decision-making tools due to accessibility of effective computers [39]. Discrete event simulation (DES) is also a flexible modeling method cha racterized by the ability to represent complex behavior within, and interactions between individuals, populations, and their environments [40]. It can mimic operations that occur in a system with the help of advanced computer and software based on some assumptions so that the system can be studied scientifically [39].

chunks.text: AAS Simulation Modeling This research will propose simulation model as part of dynamic digital twin. chunks.section: 9. CRE – Circular Economy: High -grade recycling of materials from manufacturing > 3.2. AAS Simulation Modeling
chunks.text: Flexsim uses three-dimensional (3D) visualization tha t can imitate operations very similar. In this research, Flexsim 2021 version is used. Not all version s can be used for digital twin purpose s because of communication limitation s especially for Flexsim under 2020 version, it does not support OPC UA but supports OPC Data Access (DA) and Modbus protocol. 23 In digital twin modeling, simulation modeling approach will be different compared with classical simulation modeling. It should not be valid but must be verified structurally and by definition . In the other words, it should not imitate the behavior perfectly but must imitate the structure of system. Because later on, it will be connected with physical assets in real-time.

chunks.section: 9. CRE – Circular Economy: High -grade recycling of materials from manufacturing > 3.4. Demonstration
chunks.text: In classical simulation, What -If analysis usually are used to get better decision. But it is less effective in decision making so that nowadays optimization is integrated with simulation. However, if the real condition is too dynamic, the decision ne eds to be taken fast and what-if analysis is more appropriate used rather than optimization. The process of simulation -based optimization in this research will follow iterative model [58]. Metaheuristic algorithm will give input parameters and simulation will use them to be simulated.

chunks.text: Then the results will be given back to the algorithm. After that, metaheuristic algorithm will improve it and produce new input parameters. The process will be iterated until the number of iterations reached. 24 Metaheurisitic algorithm used in this research is Genetic Algorithm (GA) by following OptQuest optimizer [59]. chunks.section: 9. CRE – Circular Economy: High -grade recycling of materials from manufacturing > 3.4. Demonstration
chunks.text: 3 Genetic Algorithm Process (Source: [60]) The scenario of s imulation-based optimization in this research will be AGV capacity planning. The idea behind it is how many goods should be brought for each AGV so that it will maximize throughput and minimize energy usage simultaneously under uncertain conditions. Since the problem does not have an analytical closed -form so that it cannot be solved with classical optimization technique or mathematical programming such as calculus or linear programming, then simulation is the one to calculate objective functions under uncertainties. The trade-off in this AGV capacity planning problem is the more goods brought in one delivery, the more energy usage needed for AGV due to the more weight and the more loading/unloading time needed . Since there are 2 objectives, then multi-objective optimization is done by using Pareto Optimality approach. This approach will give a set of optimal solutions based on Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) and users can choose based on their preferences. To select the single solution, Weighted Sum Method also will be used. The framework of simulation -based optimization for AGV Capacity Planning is shown in Figure 3.4. 25 Figure 3. 4 Framework of Simulation -based Optimization for AGV Capacity Planning Since the objectives have different unit (throughput is in unit and energy usage is in amp), therefore normalization is needed first before weighted sum method is applied to choose the best solution.

chunks.section: 1. Speed to Speed Controller
chunks.text: The structure of an AAS can be divided into a Digital Factory (DF) header and a DF body based on the concept of the DF framework benchmarked in International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standard 62832 [9]. DF header describes a list of I4.0 -compliant propertie s or usually called manifest and DF body contains a component manager .

chunks.section: 1. Speed to Speed Controller
chunks.text: DF header consists of asset identifier (Asset ID) to differ each type of asset, AAS ID to differ every AAS even in the same asset family, for example AGV 1 and AGV 2 will have different AAS ID even though they are the same asset , Number of Generic Submodels, and Number of Asset-Specific Submodels. Every ID must be unique to ensure that the information in submodels can be located appropriately and communicated between AAS in a common semantic manner so that interoperability can be realized.

chunks.section: 1. Speed to Speed Controller
chunks.text: Generic submodel in DF body means basic standardized submodel applicable to a broad variety of assets. Every AAS must include generic submodels to represent mandatory information on assets.

chunks.section: 1. Speed to Speed Controller
chunks.text: Index Data Item (IDI) submodel is the entry point of all of the other submodels which means that it is essentially a table of contents enabling efficient searching of all submodels. Property V alue Statement (PVS) submodel contains metadata that allows users to discover the attributes of the asset such as names, versions, and also documentation. Some of these properties may change along the asset lifecycle. Hence, this submodel must be upgraded regularly. Communication (CM) submodel stores informatio n about communication capabilities or communication protocol of the asset.

chunks.section: 1. Speed to Speed Controller
chunks.text: 29 When generic submodel informs static data, contrarily Asset -Specific submodel informs dynamic data containing specific information about asset functions. Different assets require different submodels to reflect specialized functions. In this manner, considering the variety and complexity of each asset function, the number of asset -specific submodels differs.

chunks.text: Simulation Model Digital twin should be started by detailed simulation modeling. Without a good simulation model, digital twin will not reflect physical system well. Before simulation model is created, the conceptual model of smart warehouse process should be clear ly described first as shown in Figure 4. 2. Layout design is shown in Figure 4. 3.

chunks.section: 1. Speed to Speed Controller > 4.2. Simulation Model
chunks.text: The flow of warehouse operations will be described as follows. When goods are arrived by truck, arrival goods will be received by forklift and goods will be sent to the Quality Control (QC) process. QC process will not generate waste products but it only checks the number and q uality of products.

chunks.section: 1. Speed to Speed Controller > 4.2. Simulation Model
chunks.text: Then, storage planning will be done to determine whether the goods will be stored in long -term storage or short-term storage. Short-term storage only stores the goods that will be sent in the same day, conversely long -term storage only stores the goods that will be sent in another day. After storage planning has been determined, Putaway process will be done by forklift either it comes from QC process to short -term storage or from long-term storage to short-term storage.

chunks.section: 1. Speed to Speed Controller > 4.2. Simulation Model
chunks.text: When the pick-up time arrives, Order picking process is done by AGVs. AGVs will pick goods directly in short -term storage in their trajectory.

chunks.section: 1. Speed to Speed Controller > 4.2. Simulation Model
chunks.text: The goods will be sent to shipping stage that consists of sorting and packaging process. Work in Process (WIP) from sorting process will be stored in the rack temporarily if the packaging process is not finished yet. Figure 4.

chunks.text: From simulation, command or control strategy can be sent to smart warehouse through cloud as well. CHAPTER 5 CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION 5.1 Conclusion The new concept of simulation -based digital twin based on Asset Administration Shell (AAS) framework has been proposed by using Flexsim software with smart warehouse as a use-case. Asset-specific submodels also have been proposed for Automated Guided Vehicle (AGV), Operator, Conveyor, Forklift, and Storage Rack.

chunks.section: 4. CHAPTER 5
chunks.text: AAS capability also has been designed which digital twin is able to monitor and control the real system as well as providing optimization . It needs OPC UA and AutomationML as c ommunication protocol and data exchange type between AAS.

chunks.section: 4. CHAPTER 5
chunks.text: The verified simulation model imitating smart warehouse has been constructed as well built in Flexsim software. It has imitated the main assets in smart warehouse as well as the layout and logic behind it.

chunks.section: 4. CHAPTER 5
chunks.text: System integration architecture also has been proposed through AAS framework and sequence diagram to help the understanding on how data and control flow from all AASs including AAS of Flexsim as digital twin. Since this research proposes simulation with Flexsim software as digital twin, two main advantages have been demonstrated. The result of simulation -based optimization for multi - objective AGV capacity planning shows that in order to maximize the total throughput and minimize energy usage simultaneously, solution ID 95 gives optimum result where the capacity for each AGV is as follows: AGV 1 (X1) = 9, AGV 2 (X2) = 9, AGV 3 (X3) = 9, AGV 4 (X4) = 8, AGV 5 (X5) = 9. This is going to be breakthrough for Digital Twin research since previous state-of-the-art analysis about DT stated that even there are still lack of DT that can reflect optimization. The result of designing dynamic dashboard also has been demonstrated to increase the capability and accuracy of controlling and monitoring such as total throughput for each product type, AGV Utilization , and Operator State.

chunks.text: 47 5.2 Recommendation Recommendation will be given for two stakeholders, namely smart warehouse and further work as follows: 1. Recommendation for smart warehouse Smart warehouse has not only a lot of assets but also movable assets that need to be analyzed carefully. This is because warehouse is an important entity in logistics.

chunks.section: 1. Recommendation for smart warehouse
chunks.text: In order to enhance smart warehouse operation, system integration through digital twin establishment based on AAS framework is very appropriate to be implemented , this research is a starting point to implement digital twin as the basic technology for system integration. Two-stage DT application has been done in this research which are system design of AAS and simulation modeling. Other warehouses also can use this proposed concept as well as methodology for establishing simulation -based digital twin that has been constructed in this research and start to apply 2 next stages which are hardware installation and PLC programming to connect digital assets and physical assets based on the proposed communication protocol . 2. Recommendation for further work In reality, there are still many lacks of industry 4.0 scenario application especially in system integration. Moreover, there is still a few researches working on AAS as the key of integration and standardization.

chunks.section: 2. Recommendation for further work
chunks.text: Since this research contributes in proposing simulation model especially Flexsim software as dynamic digital twin and have tried to consider assets a wider area, further work can start to research in the implementation stage and find efficient way. Economic analysis also should be considered in order to achieve minimum cost in implementing digital twin. Until today, it is still hard to establish standard manner to deploy digital twin without AAS.

chunks.section: 2. Recommendation for further work
chunks.text: Later on , a lot of industries can not be integrated. Without standardization, each industry will have its own digital twin and each industry will stand by itself without any integration and communication between them. That is not what industry 4.0 targeted . Moreover, this proposed concept also can be integrated with data analytics by using the same AAS framework with some additional s ubmodels. Some of data will be sent to the simulation that will be used as monitoring and controlling based on optimized decision and others will be stored in the cloud as big data to establish predictive maintenance and give the control to the physical as set automatically.
